note.text:
A point marks an exact place. We name it with a capital letter: A, B, M.

Through two points A and B we can draw exactly one straight line.
• The line (AB) has no end: it goes on forever in both directions.
• The half line [AB) starts at A, passes through B and goes on forever. A is its end point. [AB) and [BA) are different half lines.
• The line segment [AB] is the part of the line between A and B. It has two end points, A and B, and we can measure its length, written AB.

The brackets tell you the figure:
( ) no end point: a line
[ ) one end point: a half line
[ ] two end points: a segment

A straight road between two villages is like a segment. The beam of light from a torch is like a half line.

worked_example.problem: Points {P}, {Q} and {R} are on one straight line, in that order. Name the line, a segment and two half lines.
steps: The line through the three points can be called ({P}{Q}), ({P}{R}) or ({Q}{R}). They are all the same line.
[{P}{R}] is the segment with end points {P} and {R}. The point {Q} is on it.
[{Q}{R}) starts at {Q} and goes through {R}, on forever.
[{Q}{P}) also starts at {Q}, but goes the other way, through {P}. It is a different half line.

cards.idea: A point marks an exact place and is named with a capital letter. Through two points there is exactly one straight line. The line through A and B is written (AB): it has no end.
example: It goes on forever both ways, so it has no end point.

cards.idea: A half line starts at a point and goes on forever in one direction. [AB) starts at A and passes through B.
example: [{Q}{P}) starts at {Q}: it is a different half line.

cards.idea: A segment is the part of a line between two points. [AB] has two end points, and its length is written AB.
example: You can measure its length, {P}{Q}, with a ruler. A line or a half line has no length.

check.prompt: Which of these has a length you can measure?

misconceptions.explain: Lines and half lines go on forever, so they have no length. Only a segment has one.

solution: Lines and half lines go on forever, so they have no length.
Only the segment {answer} has a length you can measure.

pick.name: the half line that starts at {P} and passes through {Q}
the segment with end points {P} and {Q}

misconceptions.explain: Look at the brackets: ( ) means no end point, [ ) one end point, [ ] two end points.
A half line is named starting with its end point. [{Q}{P}) starts at {Q}, not at {P}.

solution: ( ) means no end point: a line. [ ) means one end point: a half line, named from its end point. [ ] means two end points: a segment.

questions.prompt: How many end points does {f.text} have?

misconceptions.explain: {P} and {Q} only give the figure its name. Count the square brackets: each [ or ] marks an end point.

solution: Each square bracket [ or ] marks an end point; a round bracket means the figure goes on forever.
